summary:
Our project addresses the challenge of understanding how fire behaves in microgravity. In space, flames behave differently from those on Earth, making fire risks harder to predict and manage. Research data is also difficult to review and interpret quickly.

We developed FlameLens, an AI-powered scientific platform that analyzes NASA's microgravity combustion research and datasets. It helps users explore findings, compare results, understand flame behavior, and generate useful fire-safety insights for space missions.
Our goal is to make complex research easier to understand and help researchers and engineers make better decisions about fire safety in space.
details:
FlameLens is an AI-powered scientific research platform developed for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026, Challenge 08: Flame in Freefall.

Fire behaves differently in microgravity than on Earth, making combustion behaviour and fire risks harder to understand in space. Existing scientific research is spread across complex datasets and research papers.

We developed FlameLens AI to bring this research into one interactive platform. It allows users to explore NASA combustion experiments, analyze flame behaviour, compare experimental conditions, view scientific charts, and ask an AI research assistant questions with supporting research evidence. It also provides evidence-based fire-risk indicators and research reports.

Our goal is to help researchers and engineers understand microgravity combustion more easily and support better fire-safety decisions for future space missions.

Technology Used: React, Vite, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, Python, FastAPI, Pandas, NumPy, Gemini API, ChromaDB, SQLite, PyMuPDF, and Recharts. The platform runs on standard computers and requires no special hardware.

What makes it creative: Instead of building another general-purpose chatbot, we combined scientific data analysis, experiment comparison, AI-based research assistance, and evidence-based risk assessment in one platform.

Our team considered scientific accuracy, NASA source references, data quality, uncertainty, and the difference between experimental evidence and AI-generated insights.
